npm ci --ignore-scripts run in this worktree to install locked dependencies (esbuild, tsc)
No real system clipboard read or write occurs in any test; reader and storage are in-memory fakes; a test asserts the module source does not import electron or call clipboard read/write APIs
limitations: Caller-driven capture: the service has no timers. The native or API owner must call capture() on its own polling interval while history is enabled.
Not wired into the app: no IPC channel, backend method, UI, or main-process startup code. Captain must wire the service and the Electron clipboard reader.

Secret filtering is heuristic (regex on credential shapes such as private key blocks, AWS/GitHub/Slack/Google/OpenAI-style keys, JWTs, Bearer tokens, and password/secret/api_key assignments). It reduces accidental capture and does not guarantee that no secret is stored. Credit-card and high-entropy detection are not implemented.

The concealed-content check depends on the injected reader's optional isConcealed(). The native owner must implement it using Windows clipboard formats (for example ExcludeClipboardContentFromMonitorProcessing). Without it, password-manager content is only filtered by text patterns.

Persistence is optional and plaintext when storage is injected. Without storage, history is memory only. No DPAPI or encryption is applied by this module; if persistence is enabled, the native owner should decide on encryption.
list() prunes expired entries in memory without writing to storage; the on-disk copy is pruned on the next write or on load.
A failed storage write keeps the change in memory and surfaces status().lastError. A failed read or capture is also reported through lastError rather than thrown.

Duplicate detection compares against the most recent clipboard fingerprint (SHA-256, not persisted) and against stored text. Copying the same text repeatedly while it is still on the clipboard is reported as unchanged, not as a new copy.
Entries that look sensitive are rejected at capture and also dropped when a stored document is loaded.

exports: CLIPBOARD_LIMITS: {maxEntries {min 1, max 200, default 50}, retentionMs {min 60s, max 30d, default 24h}, maxChars {min 1, max 20000, default 5000}, previewChars 120}
types: ClipboardReader, ClipboardStorage, ClipboardEntry, ClipboardEntryView, CaptureOutcome, ClipboardStatus, ClipboardHistoryOptions
interfaces.ClipboardReader: { readText(): Promise<string>; isConcealed?(): Promise<boolean> } (injected; native owner wraps the real clipboard)
interfaces.ClipboardStorage: { read(): Promise<string | null>; write(data: string): Promise<void> } (optional; atomic write expected)
interfaces.ClipboardHistoryOptions: { reader, storage?, now?: () => number (epoch ms), newId?: () => string, maxEntries?, retentionMs?, maxChars? }

methods.init(): Promise<void>. Loads persisted state when storage is provided. Call once at startup.
methods.status(): ClipboardStatus {enabled, persisted, count, maxEntries, retentionMs, maxChars, lastError?, warning?}
methods.setEnabled(on: boolean): Promise<ClipboardStatus>. Default off. Turning off purges all entries.
methods.capture(): Promise<CaptureOutcome>. Outcomes: disabled | unchanged | empty | concealed | sensitive | too-large | added | merged. Returns disabled without calling the reader when history is off.
methods.list(limit?): ClipboardEntryView[] newest first {id, preview (whitespace collapsed, max 120 chars), capturedAt, copies}. No full text.
methods.get(id): string | null. Full text for the caller to paste. The service never writes to the clipboard.
methods.purge(): Promise<void>. Removes all entries and keeps the enabled flag.

interfaces.IPC_or_API_exposure: None. Native and API owners decide what to expose. list() returns previews only; get() returns full text, so it should be gated before any renderer or API exposure.
